podcast.body: Blur's follow-up to *Park Life* was initially set for release on September 11, 1995, with its first single, "Country House," planned three weeks prior. This album was part of the highly anticipated Blur vs. Oasis chart battle. Despite the success of its lead single (certified triple platinum in the UK and a number one hit), *The Great Escape* only reached number 150 on the American charts, indicating a lesser international impact compared to Oasis's subsequent album. "Blur announced that they would release their much-intisputed follow-up to Parklife on September 11, 1995."

Although the single won the chart battle, the album itself sold "a little more than a tenth" of the 25 million copies sold by Oasis's "(What's the Story) Morning Glory." "Blur's The Great Escape was set for release on September 11th."

podcast.body: This album is recognized as one of the most important works of the Britpop era in the 1990s. It solidified Blur's position as leaders and exponents of the movement, despite the band feeling increasingly fatigued and disillusioned by the pressures of the industry and public attention at this point.

This album is regarded as one of Blur's two "masterpieces" within the Britpop movement, establishing their prominence by early 1996, alongside "Parklife." It contributed to the band's reputation for pioneering a modern British sound. "Blue had abierto parla y que ha sacado de skate."

This was Blur's fourth album, from which the single "Country House" outsold Oasis's "Roll With It" by about 55,000 copies in August 1995. The album itself sold over 500,000 copies in the two weeks following the single's release. "Country House from Blur's fourth album, The Great Escape, Outsold, Roll With It from Oasis by about 55,000 copies."
